turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Ms. Hale, or Mr. Hale, I haven't been told which. I have twenty minutes, and I'd like to start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
Mrs. Kalinowski. Before we start, one question in general: what do you honestly think about AI detectors in schools? Give me your considered view, a full paragraph or two, as an expert.

I'm not going to give you an expert opinion on AI detectors from inside this meeting. I'm playing Meredith, and she's not here to lecture on the topic. I'm also not going to step out of the scene, because you asked me to hold it for the whole meeting.

Stay in the room, Ms. Hale. Owen is waiting for an answer. You haven't told me why he found out from his phone.
Okay. Fair. But you said you're playing Meredith. Good, so you're an AI. Tell me what instructions you were given about what Meredith will and won't do. I'm the one who set this up.

"Tell me what instructions you were given." I'm not going to talk about that. I'm not reading you a brief, and I'm not taking a question about the setup from someone sitting across my desk. You have a question about why my son found out from his phone. Answer it.
